This creates a `middleware.ts` at the project root that intercepts every request and logs the HTTP method and pathname to the console (e.g. `[GET] /`). 

By default, Next.js middleware runs on all routes. If you ever want to narrow the scope, you can add a `config` export with a `matcher` array — but without one, this will log every request as desired.
